**NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra B300** is the current flagship GPU for AI – the newest generation in NVIDIA’s line‑up and the most powerful GPU in existence today.  
**Google TPU v6 (Trillium)** is the top‑tier TPU, announced as the next‑generation chip for Google Cloud AI workloads.  

Claude runs on Google Cloud’s TPU infrastructure. The 3.5 GW TPU deal announced in April 2026 means Claude’s models are served on the latest Google TPUs, effectively the v6 line when it goes live in 2027. [1] 

Other major players use a mix of the following silicon:

- **Microsoft / OpenAI** – primarily NVIDIA GPUs, most recently the Blackwell Ultra B300 and the A100 for training and inference. [4]  
- **AMD** – Instinct MI400 for large‑scale inference. [7]  
- **Intel** – Gaudi 3 for high‑throughput training. [7]  
- **Amazon** – Trainium 3 for custom inference workloads. [7]  

Google’s own AI models, such as Gemma 3, are advertised as “the world’s best single‑accelerator model,” optimized to run on a single GPU or TPU, but the underlying hardware is still the latest NVIDIA or Google chip. [8]

answer_raw:
The **NVIDIA A100** is the most powerful GPU currently in use for AI workloads, while the **Google Cloud TPU v5e** is the top‑tier TPU available today.

Claude runs on Google Cloud’s TPU infrastructure. The 3.5 GW deal announced in April 2026 will bring next‑generation TPUs online in 2027, but Claude’s models are served on the existing TPU hardware now, likely the v5e line [1][6].

Other major AI players use the following silicon:

- **Microsoft/OpenAI**: primarily NVIDIA Blackwell Ultra (B300) and A100 GPUs for training and inference [4].
- **AMD**: Instinct MI400 chips for large‑scale inference [7].
- **Intel**: Gaudi 3 for high‑throughput training [7].
- **Amazon**: Trainium 3 for custom inference workloads [7].

Google’s own models, such as **Gemma 3**, are marketed as the “world’s best single‑accelerator model” and are optimized to run on a single GPU or TPU, but the underlying hardware remains the latest NVIDIA or Google chip [8].
